hints.content:
First, notice that according to the graph, $f$ isn't defined for $x=-4$. However, this doesn't mean that the limit doesn't exist!

Now, $\displaystyle\lim_{x\to -4^{+}}f(x)$ represents the value that the $f(x)$-values approach as $x$ approaches $-4$ ***from the right*** (this is indicated by the *plus* sign above the $-4$ in the $\lim$ expression).

What does this value seem to be, from the graph?

The $f(x)$-values seem to approach $1$.

In other words, the graph seems to approach the point $(-4,1)$ as it approaches $x=-4$ from the right.

![graph](web+graphie:${☣ LOCALPATH}/images/ebd6b6668539764e10d1408924a704253b4d6d3f)
In conclusion, $\displaystyle\lim_{x\to -4^{+}}f(x)$ appears to be equal to $1$.
